learning_outcomes.text: Understanding of free and forced vibration phenomena in systems with one or more degrees of freedom.
Knowledge of mathematical modeling methods for vibrating systems.
Familiarity with analytical and numerical solutions of vibration equations.
Knowledge of techniques for reducing and controlling vibrations in mechanical and automotive applications.
Modeling and solving differential equations for vibrating systems.
Using digital and laboratory tools for vibration simulation.
Identifying and evaluating the effects of vibrations on the performance and safety of mechanical systems.
Applying criteria, evaluation methods, concepts from vibration theory in the design of mechanical systems.
Responsibility through choosing appropriate methods for vibration analysis and reduction in design.
Responsibility through complying with technical standards related to noise and vibrations.
Responsibility through proposing solutions for optimizing the operation of equipment subjected to vibrations.
Autonomy through the capacity to work independently on modeling and analyzing mechanical systems.
Autonomy through developing innovative technical solutions for complex vibration problems.
Autonomy through self-evaluation and continuous improvement of competencies through study and practice.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical vibrations: general considerations. Classification of mechanical vibrations. Elastic systems, characteristic elements. Quantities describing the vibration waveform. Vibration-medium relationship. Undamped free vibrations in systems with one degree of freedom. Flexural and torsional vibrations in systems with one degree of freedom. Elastic constants. Application.

Damped free vibrations in systems with one degree of freedom, with viscous and dry damping. Undamped forced vibrations due to harmonic excitation. Excitation by motion in undamped systems. Application.

Forced vibrations with viscous damping due to a harmonic excitation. Excitation by centrifugal force in systems with viscous damping. Transmissibility. Anti-vibration isolation. Energies in forced vibrations with viscous damping. Critical speed of shafts. Application.

Damped forced vibrations in systems with one degree of freedom, produced by any periodic excitation. Vibrations in systems with N degrees of freedom. Undamped free vibrations in systems with two degrees of freedom.

Undamped free vibrations in systems with N degrees of freedom. Determination of differential equations of vibration for systems with N degrees of freedom using Lagrange's equations. Damped vibrations in systems with N degrees of freedom. Application.
Damped vibrations in systems with N degrees of freedom. Modal analysis method. Forced vibrations with viscous damping in systems with N degrees of freedom. Torsional vibrations in gears. Application.
Approximate methods for studying vibrations of systems with a finite number of degrees of freedom. Rayleigh's method. Holzer's method. Transfer matrix method. Application.
Vibrations of continuous systems. Longitudinal vibrations of straight bars. Torsional vibrations of straight bars. Transverse vibrations of straight bars. Application.
Approximate methods in the study of continuous system vibrations. Rayleigh's method. Ritz's method. Transverse vibrations of bars with additional masses. Application.
Nonlinear vibrations. Nonlinearities in classical systems. Characteristic phenomena of nonlinear vibrations. Approximate methods for studying nonlinear vibrations.
Iteration method (Duffing). Energy balance method. Self-excited vibrations. Stability of linear systems motion. Routh-Hurwitz stability criterion.
Random vibrations. Stationary random vibrations. Autocorrelation function. Power spectral density. Shocks and transient motions.
Noise as a physical phenomenon. Acoustic pressure, acoustic pressure level. Acoustic intensity, acoustic intensity level. Vibration-noise correlation.
Combating vibrations and noise in machines and equipment. Sources of vibration and noise. Active and passive methods of control. Structures and materials used in combating vibrations and noise.
Health and safety instruction. Presentation of the Mechanical Vibrations laboratory. Anechoic chamber. Presentation of LabVIEW software.
Vibration transducers. Calibration of the measurement and vibration analysis chain.
Experimental determination of damping in an elastic system. LabVIEW application.
Simple linear dynamic absorber. Use in mechanical engineering.
Determination of natural pulsations of an elastic shaft with concentrated masses.
Vibroacoustic diagnosis and monitoring of gears and bearings.
Measurement of physical characteristics of noise generated in industrial systems.

Necessity of studying vibrations in mechanical systems. Study methods. Mathematical modeling of real physical systems. Characterization of mechanical parameters of systems with a finite number of degrees of freedom.
Free vibrations in systems with one degree of freedom.
Forced vibrations in systems with one degree of freedom.
Vibrations in systems with multiple degrees of freedom.
Vibrations in continuous systems.
Conclusions, testing, discussions.
teaching_methods: Discovery-based learning through direct and indirect exploration of reality (experiment, demonstration, modeling)

assessment_methods.method: Final evaluation (Summative evaluation test and systematic observation)
Laboratory activity (oral answers, laboratory notebook, practical demonstration)

assessment_rules: Passing requires solving well-defined, medium-complexity problems in the fundamental studied area, achieving a minimum passing score (min. 5) for the lecture component, laboratory, and seminar.
